thread.title: Spotify (SPOT) Begins Trading: What to Expect

title: Spotify (SPOT) Begins Trading: What to Expect
text:
Spotify (SPOT) Begins Trading: What to Expect April 03, 2018, 08:12:51 AM EDT By Richard Saintvilus Spotify (Getty images) 
Spotify Technology ( SPOT ), parent of Spotify, will begin trading Tuesday, bringing to fruition one of the most highly-anticipated initial public offerings this year. But investors aren’t sure what to expect. Some analysts are also in the dark, given Spotify’s unconventional listing. 
The Swedish company, which plans to offer up to 55.7 million ordinary shares, itself has warned that trading could be volatile. And that’s partly because the company has opted for a “direct listing,” which has created more than its share of uncertainty about how the stock will trade. The direct listing approach means that banker/underwriters, who typically set the initial trading price (or range) via a typical order book, won’t have any involvement. 
In this case, the direct listing will determine the opening IPO price based on orders collected from broker-dealers, completely sidestepping the traditional Wall Street process. With 159 million monthly active users and 71 million subscribers currently paying for its premium service package, Spotify is no-doubt a tech heavyweight. This is yet one example of how the company seems unafraid to do things its own way. 
Still, Spotify’s IPO comes at a time when tech stocks, lead by FAANGs — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) — are taking massive hits to their market caps. What’s more, Spotify will begin trading at time when analysts, citing competitive pressures from Apple, predict Spotify will soon lose its No. 1 music streaming status as early as this summer. 
While Apple Music, which is only three years old, is growing its U.S. user base at a rate of 5% per month. Spotify, which has had a ten-year lead, is growing at a rate of only 2%, according to The Wall Street Journal. And the heated competition extends beyond Apple. Aside from Amazon’s Alexa-powered music service, there’s also Google’s YouTube, which boasts a subscriber base of 70 million. And to say nothing about Pandora ( P ), which has undertaken an organizational restructuring aimed at strengthening its finances and growth position. 
Despite the recent downdraft for Big Tech shares on Wall Street, analysts believe Spotify’s IPO will be a success, given that last year it reported revenue of $4.99 billion, which grew almost 40% year over year. And it expects 2018 revenue in the range of $6.1 billion to $6.8 billion, marking an almost 30% increase at the mid-point. These growth trends excite analysts at MKM Partners, who has initiated coverage on the stock with a price target of $200 per share. 
Sean Stiefel, a portfolio manager at Navy Capital, is also excited about Spotify’s prospects, saying, “There is a lot of appetite [for the stock] here.” Adding, “So far at least they have emerged as the go-to smartphone music service ahead of Pandora, YouTube and Amazon.” 
What the trading range will be when the stock opens for trading (likely mid afternoon Tuesday) will be anyone’s guess. Spotify, in its most recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 23, said private shares traded in a price range of $48.93 to $132.50 between Jan. 1 through March 9. Analysts have pegged the company’s market valuation to be in a range of $16 billion to $23 billion. And given the bullish sentiment about the company, that valuation range could go much higher.
